newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL share index ends down 2.42 pct to 5-1/2 mth low.
newsitem.headline: KL share index ends down 2.42 pct to 5-1/2 mth low.

text.p: Malaysian shares fell for the sixth straight session, with the benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index falling 2.42 percent to close at a five-and-a-half-month low of 1,152.51.
Dealers and analysts said market sentiment remained weak after overnight losses on Wall Street and credit tightening measures announced by Bank Negara last week.
The closing level was the lowest for the Composite Index since October 15 last year when it ended at 1,156.40.
Dealers said shares were also pulled down by lack of support from funds and calls by broking houses to clients who had bought shares on credit to top up their margins.
"There's a lot of margin calls and not much institutional support," said Tony Shue, an institutional dealer at Jupiter Securities.
He said the benchmark index had reached a level that "nobody knows where it's going next. It could fall by another 20 to 30 points."
